mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% q/q over last 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS rises >0.25% q/q.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 8% triggers widespread cost-cutting and reduced consumer confidence, depressing earnings and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 8%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals broad-based supply weakness, which reduces corporate margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained industrial production contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous and persistent rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of higher rates and inflation, eroding real corporate earnings and pushing S&P 500 returns lower over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12-mo avg AND CPIAUCSL > 12-mo avg for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A strong and sustained increase in personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average, without a corresponding rise in consumption (GDPC1), signals a savings-driven environment that depresses near-term corporate demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-mo avg for 3 months AND GDPC1 < 12-mo avg for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS rises and GDPC1 lags for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the household survey unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% for more than six months signals an extremely tight labor market, which raises wage inflation and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE remains below 5% for more than six months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a recovery in residential investment, which boosts construction-related sectors and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST exceeds its 12-month average for four consecutive months.
